Class UserRegister

java.lang.Object
edu.ntnu.idi.bidata.UserRegister
public class UserRegister extends Object
Registry class for managing users in the diary application.

Role and Responsibility

The UserRegister class is responsible for managing a collection of User objects while they are in the application.

Key Responsibilities:
  • User registration: Creating new users with password hashing
  • Authentication: Verifying login credentials
  • User lookup: Finding users by username
  • Persistence: Saving and loading users to/from JSON files
  • Password security: Providing hashing for passwords
  • Author statistics: Displaying entry counts per author
Information Stored and Data Type Justification

This class stores:

  • List of Users (userList): A list of users. ArrayList was chosen because:
    • The number of users is unknown at startup and grows as users register
    • Users need to be iterated through for login verification and lookups
    • Stream operations provide clean, functional-style querying
    • Easy serialisation/deserialisation with Gson library
  • gson (Gson): A standard Gson instance is used because:
    • User objects don't contain LocalDateTime (unlike DiaryEntry), so no custom adapter is needed
    • Gson handles Author and String fields automatically
Mutability Assessment

The userList and the gson is set by the constructor. Both are final and wont be changed later. Only the content of the userList will change.

Invalid Data Handling Strategy

This class uses a combination of graceful degradation, exception propagation, and boolean return values

  • Constructor Details

    • UserRegister

      public UserRegister()
      Creates a new empty UserRegister.

      Initalises an empty user list (ArrayList) and a standard Gson instance for JSON operations. Users can be added via addNewUser() or loaded from file via readFromJSON()

  • Method Details

    • hash

      public static String hash(String text)
      Methods which hashes a string using SHA-256 algorithm and returns it as a Base64-encoding string.

      This method is used to hash passwords so that it can be stored securely. The acctual password cannot be recovered from the hash.

      Parameters:
      text - the string to be hashed (in our case a password)
      Returns:
      the hashed text as a Base64-encoded string
      Throws:
      RuntimeException - if the SHA-256 algorithm is not avaliable on the system.

    • addNewUser

      public void addNewUser(String name, String username, String password)
      Creating and registrating a new user in the system.

      Creates an Author object with a combined name-username idetifyer, hashes the password for secure storage, creates a new user and adds it to the register.

      Parameters:
      name - the display name of the user
      username - the distinct username for login
      password - the password in plain text (this will be hashed before storage)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if username or password is blank (thrown by User constructor)

    • isUser

      public boolean isUser(String username)
      Checks if the username belongs to an existing user within the system.

      The comparison is case-insensitive

      Parameters:
      username - The username to check
      Returns:
      true (the user exists) or false (otherwise)

    • login

      public boolean login(String username, String password)
      Authenticates a user by verifying their username and password.

      The password is hashed and compared against the stored hash. Username comparison is case insensitive.

      Parameters:
      username - The username to authenticate
      password - The password in plain text to verify
      Returns:
      true (if the username and the password matches) or false (otherwise)

    • getByUsername

      public User getByUsername(String username)

      Returns:

    • printAuthorStatistics

      public void printAuthorStatistics()
      Printing the author statistics to console.

      Displays each author's name and the number of diary entries they have written.

    • readFromJson

      public void readFromJson()
      Reads users from the JSON file "users.json" into the user list.

      If the file does not exist, no action is taken to allow a fresh start. If the file is exists but is empty or invalid an error message is printed, but the program continues.

    • writeToJson

      public void writeToJson()
      Writes all users to the JSON file "users.json".

      Overwrites any existing file content.

      Error handeling:
      Uses graceful degradiation if writing fails an error message is printed to console, but the application continue running
